newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shell Singapore cuts refining, impact seen small.
newsitem.headline: Shell Singapore cuts refining, impact seen small.

text.p: Shell Singapore said on Monday it would cut refining output, but the decision was unlikely to have have much impact on profits or prices in a glutted market, industry sources said.

Shell, Singapore's largest refiner announced a near seven percent cut in production atits refinery on Pulau Bukom, which has a capcity of its 430,000 barrel per day (bpd), or 59,000 tonne per day (TPD).
"It is a drop in the bucket when you look at the regional refining capacity. The storage tanks in Singapore look quite full and there isn't much demand out there," one refining source said.

"As a response to market condition, the plan is to achieve an average of 57,000 TPD for the month and this will entail production cuts in the second half of the month," Shell said in written reply to a Reuters query.
The lower production target for June will lead to a cut in output of 4,000 TPD cut.
Esso Singapore cut output by 10 percent on May 27 at its 230,000 bpd refinery, a source close to the company told Reuters earlier. An Esso spokeswoman, however, declined comment.

Singapore's four refineries produce nearly 1.3 million bpd of refined products. Despite its low volume compared to Asia's 17 million bpd, the centre is Asia's swing refiner, and as such, the region's key refining barometer.
The two other refiners, Mobil Oil and Singapore Refining Co (SRC), are not expected to cut output in the immediate future due to different internal requirements.

Mobil, with a 300,000 bpd refining capacity, needs to maintain production to ensure sufficient feedstock for a new lube base oil plant due to start production in the third quarter, a company source said.
SRC is not cutting back output due to the differing needs of its shareholders despite facing storage problems at its 280,000 bpd refinery, a source close to the company said.
The company is a joint venture between British Petroleum, Singapore Petroleum Corp and Caltex, itself a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
Traders said the cuts by Esso and Shell gave the impression that refiners are doing something about low product prices, but reality it will not have much impact.
"The market is dominated by arbitrage cargoes. There is little these refiners can do about this and we have to wait for all these cargoes to be absorbed before things improve," one trader said.
Refining profits in Singapore sank into the red in late May when oil product prices fell under the weight of huge exports from the West seeking Asia's higher prices.
At that time, refiners were losing up to $1.00 for every barrel refined at the basic stage but margins have since improved to yield profits of between 50 cents to $1.00.
But the improved returns are not leading to higher operations because the refiners are having trouble finding a market for their product and stocks in Singapore are rising.
Data from the Trade Development Board showed middle distillate stocks in the week ending June 11 rose 993,000 barrels to 11.236 million barrels, the highest since at least January 1994.
Traders said unless an outlet emerges for these cargoes, prices wouldl continue to slide.
